## The method works: the road to IceCube {#method-works}

::::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{=html}
<div class="timing" style="font-size: 1em; grid-template-columns: 9rem 1fr;">
<span class="time">1996</span><span>Baikal NT96: a clear upward-going neutrino signal</span>
<span class="time">1998</span><span>Baikal NT200 completed with 192 optical modules</span>
<span class="time">1990s</span><span>AMANDA: deeper ice makes directional reconstruction possible</span>
<span class="time">1999</span><span>The AMANDA team proposes a cubic-kilometre detector, IceCube</span>
<span class="time">then</span><span>Funding for construction is granted</span>
<span class="time">2004–05</span><span>First IceCube construction season</span>
<span class="time">2010</span><span>The last of 86 strings</span>
<span class="time">2013</span><span>An astrophysical neutrino flux</span>
</div>
```

Atmospheric neutrinos showed that Markov's method works, in a lake and in ice.
